systems.name: Sol System
systems.spectral_summary: G2V Yellow Dwarf · 8 Planets · 11 Major Moons
systems.description: Our home planetary system: the G2V star Sol, four rocky inner worlds, the main Asteroid Belt, four giant outer worlds, Pluto-Charon, and their major moons.

systems.name: Alpha Centauri
systems.spectral_summary: G2V + K1V + M5.5Ve Triple Star · Proxima b
systems.description: The closest star system to Earth at 4.37 light-years: the bright binary pair Rigil Kentaurus (A) and Toliman (B), orbited by red dwarf Proxima Centauri and rocky exoplanet Proxima b.

systems.name: Barnard's Star
systems.description: An ancient, fast-moving red dwarf 5.96 light-years from Sol, orbited closely by the frozen rocky sub-Earth Barnard b.

systems.name: Sirius
systems.spectral_summary: A1V Blue-White Star + DA2 White Dwarf
systems.description: The brightest star in Earth’s night sky. Sirius A blazes 25 times brighter than the Sun alongside its ultra-dense white dwarf companion Sirius B.

systems.name: Epsilon Eridani
systems.spectral_summary: K2V Orange Dwarf · Debris Disk · AEgir
systems.description: A young, magnetically active K-type star wrapped in shimmering asteroid belts and orbited by the Jovian gas giant AEgir.

systems.name: Tau Ceti
systems.spectral_summary: G8V Sun-like Dwarf · Super-Earths e & f
systems.description: A serene, metal-poor Sun-like star hosting candidate habitable-zone super-Earths Tau Ceti e and icy outer world Tau Ceti f.

systems.name: Vega
systems.spectral_summary: A0Va Oblate Blue-White Star · Dust Ring
systems.description: A rapidly spinning sapphire-white star flattened at its poles, encircled by an expansive luminous circumstellar dust ring.

systems.name: TRAPPIST-1
systems.spectral_summary: M8V Ultra-Cool Dwarf · Compact Temperate Worlds
systems.description: An ultra-cool crimson dwarf with tightly packed Earth-sized rocky worlds—standing on TRAPPIST-1e, neighboring planets loom larger than Earth’s Moon.

systems.name: Betelgeuse
systems.description: A colossal pulsing red supergiant nearing the end of its stellar life, billowing gigantic convective plasma cells across Orion.

systems.name: Sagittarius A*
systems.spectral_summary: Supermassive Black Hole · 4.3M Solar Masses · Galactic Core
systems.description: The colossal supermassive black hole anchoring the heart of the Milky Way. Spacetime bends violently around its 24-million-km Event Horizon, lensing starlight and a searing relativistic accretion disk into impossible twin arches.

bodies.name: Sun (Sol)
bodies.summary: G2V main-sequence star containing 99.86% of the Solar System’s mass. Surface photosphere burns at 5,778 K.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.summary: Innermost sun-baked world scarred by Caloris Basin, towering lobate scarps, and deep polar shadowed craters.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.summary: Shrouded in golden sulfuric-acid cloud decks with 92-bar crushing greenhouse pressure and volcanic basalt plains.

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.summary: Dynamic ocean world protected by a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere, magnetosphere, swirling weather fronts, and thriving biosphere.

bodies.name: Moon (Luna)
bodies.summary: Earth’s tidally locked companion: ancient basaltic maria, luminous ejecta rays of Tycho, and crisp one-sixth gravity.

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.summary: The Red Planet: iron-oxide deserts, colossal Olympus Mons shield volcano, Valles Marineris canyon, and CO₂ polar ice caps.

bodies.name: Phobos
bodies.summary: Grooved, dark carbonaceous inner moon skimming just 6,000 km above Mars’s rusty horizon, dominated by Stickney Crater.

bodies.name: Deimos
bodies.summary: Smooth regolith-blanketed outer Martian moon offering serene views of Mars hanging silently against the stars.

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.summary: King of the planets: turbulent ammonia cloud belts, counter-rotating jet streams, and the centuries-old Great Red Spot.

bodies.name: Io
bodies.summary: The most volcanically active world in the Solar System, painted in sulfur plains and dark silicate lava calderas by Jupiter’s tides.

bodies.name: Europa
bodies.summary: Luminous fractured water-ice crust scored with reddish salt lineae concealing a vast global subsurface ocean.

bodies.name: Ganymede
bodies.summary: Largest moon in the Solar System—larger than Mercury—with ancient dark regions, bright grooved ice, and its own magnetosphere.

bodies.name: Callisto
bodies.summary: A primordial, heavily cratered ice-rock world speckled with glistening frost rims and the vast multi-ring Valhalla basin.

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.summary: Jewel of the outer Solar System: pale golden atmospheric bands crowned by sweeping water-ice rings and the Cassini Division.

bodies.name: Enceladus
bodies.summary: Reflective snow-white ice moon whose southern tiger-stripe fractures erupt water-ice plumes feeding Saturn’s E ring.

bodies.name: Titan
bodies.summary: Saturn’s giant moon cloaked in dense golden nitrogen-methane haze above hydrocarbon dunes and cryogenic methane seas.

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.summary: Pale aquamarine ice giant rolling nearly sideways on a 97.8° tilt with delicate vertical dark-dust rings.

bodies.name: Titania
bodies.summary: Uranus’s largest moon: pale icy-rock plains sliced by Messina Chasmata fault canyons over 1,500 km long.

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.summary: Deep cobalt ice giant whipped by supersonic 2,100 km/h winds and bright high-altitude frozen methane cirrus clouds.

bodies.name: Triton
bodies.summary: Captured Kuiper Belt world orbiting Neptune backwards, covered in cantaloupe terrain and pink nitrogen-ice geysers.

bodies.name: Pluto
bodies.summary: Kuiper Belt dwarf planet featuring the bright nitrogen glacier Sputnik Planitia (Tombaugh Regio) and tenuous blue nitrogen haze.

bodies.name: Charon
bodies.summary: Pluto’s mutually tidally locked binary partner with dramatic equatorial chasms and the dark reddish Mordor Macula polar cap.

bodies.name: Alpha Centauri A
bodies.summary: Rigil Kentaurus: a luminous G2V star 1.5× brighter than the Sun, forming a close gravitational binary with Alpha Centauri B.

bodies.name: Alpha Centauri B
bodies.summary: Toliman: a golden-amber K1V orange dwarf shining warmly across the skies of the Centauri system.

bodies.name: Centauri Prime (Chiron)
bodies.summary: A candidate warm ringed giant bathed in twin-sun light within the Alpha Centauri A habitable zone.

bodies.name: Aethel (Exomoon)
bodies.summary: Temperate emerald-teal exomoon orbiting under Chiron’s luminous ice rings and the twin suns of Alpha Centauri.

bodies.name: Proxima Centauri
bodies.summary: The nearest individual star to the Sun at 4.24 light-years: a flare-active crimson dwarf hosting confirmed rocky worlds.

bodies.name: Proxima Centauri b
bodies.summary: Closest known exoplanet to Earth—a rocky super-Earth in Proxima’s habitable zone with an amber twilight terminator belt.

bodies.name: Proxima Centauri d
bodies.summary: Sub-Earth rocky world skimming perilously close to Proxima Centauri’s crimson flares.

bodies.name: Barnard's Star
bodies.summary: Ten-billion-year-old red dwarf racing through the local solar neighborhood faster than any other star in Earth’s sky.

bodies.name: Barnard b
bodies.summary: Ancient wind-scoured sub-Earth rocky world illuminated by the deep ember glow of Barnard’s Star.

bodies.name: Sirius A
bodies.summary: Brilliant blue-white A-type star burning at 9,940 K—the brightest beacon in Earth’s night sky.

bodies.name: Sirius B (White Dwarf)
bodies.summary: Earth-sized degenerate stellar core packing the mass of the entire Sun at 25,000 K surface temperature.

bodies.name: Sirius I (Cinder)
bodies.summary: Obsidian-basalt world glowing with magma fissures beneath the blinding ultraviolet radiance of Sirius A.

bodies.name: Epsilon Eridani
bodies.summary: Young 800-million-year-old orange dwarf surrounded by dense asteroid belts and active planet formation.

bodies.name: AEgir (Eps Eri b)
bodies.summary: Confirmed Jovian exoplanet carving lanes through Epsilon Eridani’s luminous debris disks.

bodies.name: Ran (Exomoon)
bodies.summary: Tidally heated rocky moon circling AEgir amid amber dust plumes and warm starlight.

bodies.name: Tau Ceti
bodies.summary: Single, remarkably stable Sun-like G8V star long studied as a prime candidate for habitable worlds.

bodies.name: Tau Ceti e
bodies.summary: Warm super-Earth at the inner edge of Tau Ceti’s habitable zone with turquoise archipelagos and sweeping trade-wind cloud bands.

bodies.name: Tau Ceti f
bodies.summary: Glacial super-Earth along the outer habitable edge, sculpted by vast crystalline ice sheets and crisp blue twilight.

bodies.name: Vega
bodies.summary: Rapidly rotating sapphire-white beacon in Lyra encircled by an immense luminous dust ring.

bodies.name: Lyra-1 (Dust World)
bodies.summary: Silicate-glass desert world bathed in crystalline blue-white Vegian starlight inside Vega’s inner dust gap.

bodies.name: TRAPPIST-1
bodies.summary: Jupiter-sized ultra-cool red dwarf anchoring a breathtakingly compact chain of seven Earth-sized rocky worlds.

bodies.name: TRAPPIST-1d
bodies.summary: Compact warm rocky world where neighboring TRAPPIST-1e rises hugely across the crimson twilight sky.

bodies.name: TRAPPIST-1e
bodies.summary: Prime habitable-zone ocean-continent exoplanet with iron-rich core, liquid seas, and dramatic sister worlds hanging overhead.

bodies.name: TRAPPIST-1f
bodies.summary: Water-rich glacier planet glimmering pale rose-white under the soft infrared warmth of TRAPPIST-1.

bodies.name: Betelgeuse
bodies.summary: Colossal red supergiant wide enough to swallow Mars’s orbit, churning with planet-sized boiling convective cells.

bodies.name: Sagittarius A*
bodies.summary: Supermassive Kerr black hole at the Milky Way core. Relativistic light bending wraps its incandescent accretion disk over and under an absolute pitch-black Event Horizon.

bodies.name: Star S2
bodies.summary: A blazing blue-white massive star whipping around Sagittarius A* at 7,650 km/s—nearly 2.5% the speed of light—proving general relativistic gravitational redshift.

bodies.name: Penrose's Edge
bodies.summary: A dark obsidian world locked in deep gravitational time dilation—stand on its fractured lava plains to witness Sagittarius A* towering across the warped sky.
